elements.element: Customer is not prohibited from participating in competing or similar projects or otherwise using alternative providers.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 prohibits the Company for 12 months from participating in any similar Internet project concerning Deerskin Products.

elements.element: Vendor is not granted any exclusive or sole-supplier right that restricts Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 grants HDI the exclusive right to use the Deerskin brand for a consumer-facing Deerskin Products website.

elements.element: Any Customer exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: The restriction is expressly limited to the identified category “Deerskin Products”; the broader restriction covering substantially similar products was removed.

elements.element: Any Customer exclusivity lasts no more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 limits exclusivity to the 12-month period commencing on the Effective Date, notwithstanding the Agreement’s renewal provisions.

elements.element: Customer exclusivity terminates automatically upon Vendor's failure to meet applicable service levels.
elements.evidence: The service-related trigger applies only to failures of material obligations under Sections 1 or 5 that remain uncured for 30 days after Company notice. It does not terminate exclusivity upon the Vendor’s failure to meet an applicable service level.

elements.element: Customer exclusivity terminates automatically upon Vendor's failure to meet applicable delivery dates.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly covers only failure to make the Site operational within the Section 1.6 launch period. It does not cover failures to meet all applicable delivery dates, and other Section 1 or 5 failures are subject to materiality, notice, and a 30-day cure period.

result.reason: The redline narrows exclusivity to Deerskin Products and 12 months, but it retains an exclusivity obligation and does not provide the fallback’s required automatic termination upon each service-level or delivery-date failure. Its performance exit is materially narrowed by materiality, notice, and cure conditions, while its delivery-date protection expressly identifies only the launch deadline. The changes remain confined to the related exclusivity mechanics and do not disturb the separate term, renewal, or termination-payment provisions.
